children.prompt: Tyrion worked 17 hours and earned \$328.10. Find his hourly wage rate.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Pay per period} &= \frac{\text{Total pay}}{\text{Number of periods}}\\\text{Hourly wage rate} &= \frac{\$328.10}{17\text{ hours}}\\\text{Hourly wage rate} &= \$19.30/\text{h}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Abigaile worked 29 hours and earned \$700.07. Find her hourly wage rate. Give your answer to the nearest cent.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Pay per period} &= \frac{\text{Total pay}}{\text{Number of periods}}\\\text{Hourly wage rate} &= \frac{\$700.07}{29\text{ hours}}\\\text{Hourly wage rate} &\approx \$24.14/\text{h}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Seb earned \$3078 over 3 weeks. Each week he works 38 hours. How much does he get paid per hour?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Total hours} &= 38\times3=114\\\text{Pay per period} &= \frac{\text{Total pay}}{\text{Number of periods}}\\\text{Hourly wage rate} &= \frac{\$3078}{114\text{ hours}}\\\text{Hourly wage rate} &= \$27/\text{h}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Chloe earned \$2349.60 this fortnight. She works 40 hours per week. What is her hourly wage rate?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Total hours} &= 40\times2=80\\\text{Pay per period} &= \frac{\text{Total pay}}{\text{Number of periods}}\\\text{Hourly wage rate} &= \frac{\$2349.60}{80\text{ hours}}\\\text{Hourly wage rate} &= \$29.37/\text{h}\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Hours}&=\frac{\text{Total pay}}{\text{Pay per hour}}\\\text{Hours}&=\frac{2000}{21.45}\\\text{Hours}&\approx93.24\end{align*}$$
It would take approximately $93.24$ hours.

How long would it take him to earn enough to buy a phone costing \$1800? Give the number of hours to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Hours}&=\frac{\text{Total pay}}{\text{Pay per hour}}\\\text{Hours}&=\frac{1800}{35.65}\\\text{Hours}&\approx50.49\end{align*}$$
It would take approximately $50.49$ hours. Keep $\frac{1800}{35.65}$ unrounded for the next calculation.

children.prompt: If he works 6 hours per week, how many weeks would this take? Give the number of weeks to 3 decimal places. Use the unrounded number of hours.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Weeks}&=\frac{\text{Total hours}}{\text{Hours per week}}\\\text{Weeks}&=\frac{1800/35.65}{6}\\\text{Weeks}&\approx8.415\end{align*}$$
It would take approximately $8.415$ weeks.

children.label: d
children.prompt:
Cathy earns \$60/hr.
How many weeks would it take her to earn enough for \$2400, if she works 4.5 hours per week?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Hours}&=\frac{\text{Total pay}}{\text{Pay per hour}}\\\text{Hours}&=\frac{2400}{60}\\\text{Hours}&=40\\\text{Weeks}&=\frac{\text{Total hours}}{\text{Hours per week}}\\\text{Weeks}&=\frac{40}{4.5}\\\text{Weeks}&=\frac{80}{9}=8.\overline{8}\end{align*}$$
It would take $8.\overline{8}$ weeks.

How much did Rose earn last week? Give your answer to the nearest cent.

answer.worked:
Rose works 4 hours on each of five weekdays, 2.5 hours on Saturday and 3 hours on Sunday.
$$\begin{align*}
\text{Normal hours} &= 5\times4=20\text{ h}\\
\text{Normal pay} &= 24.05\times20=\$481.00\\
\text{Saturday pay} &= 24.05\times2.5\times1.5=\$90.1875\\
\text{Sunday pay} &= 24.05\times3\times2=\$144.30\\
\text{Total pay} &= 481+90.1875+144.30\\
\text{Total pay} &= \$715.4875\approx\$715.49
\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: Jeffrey earns \$5205.50 per month. Calculate how much he earns per: Give answers to the nearest cent where necessary.

answer.worked:
There are 12 months in a year.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Annual pay} &= \$5205.50\times12\\\text{Annual pay} &= \$62\,466\end{align*}$$

Convert to annual pay, then divide by 52 weeks.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Annual pay} &= \$5205.50\times12\\\text{Annual pay} &= \$62\,466\\\text{Weekly pay} &= \frac{\$62\,466}{52}\\\text{Weekly pay} &\approx \$1201.27\end{align*}$$

Convert to annual pay, then divide by 26 fortnights.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Annual pay} &= \$5205.50\times12\\\text{Annual pay} &= \$62\,466\\\text{Fortnightly pay} &= \frac{\$62\,466}{26}\\\text{Fortnightly pay} &\approx \$2402.54\end{align*}$$

sourceAtom.visibleSubtitle: A tax misconception.

inlines.text: Your friend currently earns $119,000 a year. She is about to get a $3000 pay rise.
In which tax bracket is she in currently?

answer.worked: \$119,000 lies in the third bracket, \$45,001–\$120,000. Its marginal tax rate is 32.5%.

inlines.text: In which tax bracket will she be in afterwards?

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}\text{New income}&=119\,000+3000\\&=\$122\,000\end{align*}$
\$122,000 lies in the fourth bracket, \$120,001–\$180,000. Its marginal tax rate is 37%.

inlines.text: Your friend says: “I don’t want the pay rise. The government will start taxing me at 37%, rather than 32.5%, which means I’ll have less money than before!”
Explain to your friend why she is incorrect, using mathematical reasoning:

answer.short: Third bracket; excess \$74,000; tax \$29,142; after-tax income \$89,858.
Income \$122,000; fourth bracket; excess \$2000; tax \$30,207; after-tax income \$91,793.

inlines.text: The new tax rate is only on each

answer.short: Additional. Only income above \$120,000 is taxed at 37%; her after-tax income increases by \$1935.
answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}\text{Increase in after-tax income}&=91\,793-89\,858\\&=\$1935\end{align*}$
She has more money after the pay rise. The first \$1000 of the rise is taxed at 32.5%, and the remaining \$2000 is taxed at 37%. The 37% rate applies only to additional dollars above \$120,000; it does not apply to her whole income.

content.prompt:
Theo is completing his tax return.
He has a gross salary of \$82 521 and income from a rental property totalling \$10 920.
He is claiming \$13 420 in allowable deductions.

inlines.text: Using the tax table below, calculate Theo’s tax payable.
Give monetary answers to the nearest cent.

answer.worked:
The taxable income is in the \$80 001–\$180 000 bracket.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Excess} &= 80\,021-80\,000\\\text{Excess} &= \$21\\\text{Income tax} &= 17\,547+0.37\times21\\\text{Income tax} &= \$17\,554.77\end{align*}$$

children.prompt:
In addition to the above tax, Theo must also pay a Medicare levy of \$1600.42.
Theo has already paid \$20 525 as Pay as You Go (PAYG) tax.
Should Theo receive a tax refund, or will he owe more tax? Justify your answer.

answer.short: Refund of \$1369.81; PAYG paid exceeds total tax payable.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total tax payable} &= 17\,554.77+1600.42\\\text{Total tax payable} &= \$19\,155.19\\\text{Instalments}-\text{Total tax payable} &= 20\,525-19\,155.19\\\text{Instalments}-\text{Total tax payable} &= \$1369.81\end{align*}$$
Theo receives a refund of \$1369.81 because his PAYG payments exceed his total tax payable.

teachingContext.method: Gross income minus allowable deductions; round taxable income down to whole dollars.
Find the bracket, calculate excess over the previous bracket limit, then use base tax plus rate times excess.
Add the Medicare levy to income tax to obtain total tax payable.
Round completed monetary stages to cents; subtract total tax payable from instalments to determine a refund or liability.

inlines.text: The table shows the tax payable to the Australian Taxation Office for different taxable incomes.
Peta has a gross annual salary of $84 000.
She has tax deductions of $1000 for work-related travel and $500 for stationery.
The Medicare levy that she pays is calculated at 1.5% of her taxable income.
Peta has already paid $18 500 in tax.
Will Peta receive a tax refund, or will she owe money to the Australian Taxation Office?
Justify your answer by calculating the refund or amount owed.
Round each calculated income-tax and Medicare-levy amount to the nearest cent before combining them.

answer.short: Peta owes \$1209.50; total tax payable is \$19 709.50.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Taxable income} &= 84\,000-(1000+500)\\\text{Taxable income} &= \$82\,500\end{align*}$$
The taxable income is in the \$80 001–\$180 000 bracket.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Excess} &= 82\,500-80\,000\\\text{Excess} &= \$2500\\\text{Income tax} &= 17\,547+0.37\times2500\\\text{Income tax} &= \$18\,472.00\\\text{Medicare levy} &= 0.015\times82\,500\\\text{Medicare levy} &= \$1237.50\\\text{Total tax payable} &= 18\,472.00+1237.50\\\text{Total tax payable} &= \$19\,709.50\\\text{Instalments}-\text{Total tax payable} &= 18\,500-19\,709.50\\\text{Instalments}-\text{Total tax payable} &= -\$1209.50\end{align*}$$
Peta owes \$1209.50 because her tax payments are less than her total tax payable.

1 year = 12 months (per annum p.a. means per year)
= 52 weeks
= 26 fortnights

If you underpay, you have a tax liability. You owe the government money.

entries.description: MEDICARE LEVY

• Medicare is the Australian universal healthcare scheme. When you go to the doctor, the cost of the visit is either free, or the government will pay for a large percentage of the cost.
• The government partly gets its money from an additional tax called the Medicare levy.

Medicare Levy
Medicare Levy = 2% × Taxable Income
Total tax payable = Income tax payable + Medicare levy
